exposure: Maternal self-reported preterm birth (<37 weeks' gestation)
Maternal self-reported postterm birth (>42 weeks' gestation)
outcome: Validity (assessed by sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, Cohen's kappa, paired t-test, Pearson's correlation coefficient, Bland-Altman plots)
cohort: The participants were 715 mothers from Bergen, Norway, who provided questionnaire data from the RHINE III study regarding their 1629 births that occurred between 1967 and 2010.
finding: Maternally reported birth and pregnancy information demonstrated high validity for important parameters like child's gender and caesarean section, good agreement for instrumental delivery and extremely preterm birth, moderate agreement for preterm birth and induction of labour, and was independent of recall time over 45 years.
mod_finding: Caesarean section showed a high degree of validity (kappa = 0.99, sensitivity and specificity 100%), while instrumental delivery (forceps and vacuum) showed good agreement with sensitivity 75-92%.
followup_time: Recall time up to 45 years (for births between 1967 and 2010)
cross-section timing: N/A (The study validated retrospectively collected self-reported data on births occurring between 1967 and 2010.)
birth_weight: N/A (Birthweight was a variable assessed for validity, not a criterion for inclusion of the cohort)
gest_age: N/A (Gestational age categories like preterm birth [<37 weeks] and postterm birth [>42 weeks] were variables assessed for validity, not criteria for inclusion of the cohort)
